name: Tallgrass prairie
notes: Warm-season C4 bunchgrasses 1-3 m tall with forbs, fire-maintained, trees only as bur-oak savanna edges; North American Great Plains east (Iowa, Kansas, Illinois) with Pampas/Eurasian meadow-steppe analogues.

canopy.name: Bur oak
canopy.source: Quercus macrocarpa, central/eastern N America, fire-tolerant savanna oak, 15-30 m — USDA PLANTS / Flora of North America

shrub.name: Leadplant
shrub.source: Amorpha canescens, Great Plains tallgrass prairie, deep-rooted legume shrub 0.5-1 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Prairie rose
shrub.source: Rosa arkansana, central N America prairies, low suckering shrub to 0.6 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: American hazel
shrub.source: Corylus americana, eastern/central N America, thicket shrub 2-4 m at prairie-woodland edge — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Pampas grass
shrub.source: Cortaderia selloana, S American Pampas, tussock grass with 3 m plumes — Flora Argentina / Kew POWO

ground.name: Big bluestem
ground.source: Andropogon gerardii, dominant tallgrass prairie grass, central N America, 1.5-2.5 m, turns bronze in autumn — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Indiangrass
ground.source: Sorghastrum nutans, N American tallgrass co-dominant, golden plumes, 1-2 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Switchgrass
ground.source: Panicum virgatum, N American prairies and lowlands, 1-2 m bunchgrass — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Little bluestem
ground.source: Schizachyrium scoparium, N American prairies on drier upland soils, 0.5-1 m, red-brown in autumn — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Compass plant
ground.source: Silphium laciniatum, tallgrass prairie forb with yellow sunflower heads, 1.5-3 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Purple coneflower
ground.source: Echinacea purpurea, central/eastern N America prairie forb, 0.6-1.2 m — USDA PLANTS
